summary: Added the SHARD MODEL to the Totem pipeline (Tracey directive) - and dogfooded it: this very entry is the first lane Totem, written to pod/totems/shards/totems.claude.jsonl, so the trunk totems.jsonl is never touched while Codex is mid-write (the exact race the shard model removes). A single shared totems.jsonl is a single-writer format with two race points under parallel SI work: the monotonic id (both agents reach for the same next number - seen live this session: Codex took 0036, I took 0037; then the 0039 head/tail split) and the file itself (two appends can interleave mid-line). The fix is LANES: one append-only file per writer under pod/totems/shards/ named totems.<lane>.jsonl, ids TOTEM-<LANE>-<NNNN> (lane-local numbers - never compared across lanes), and the canonical ledger is the MERGE of the legacy trunk + every lane ordered by utc (trunk wins ties), computed at read time so there is no shared file to contend on. verify_totems.py is now shard-aware: it loads totems.jsonl + all shards/totems.*.jsonl, merges by utc, and runs the SAME latest-wins-per-file over that one time-ordered sequence; with no shards it behaves identically to before (backward compatible). totem.schema.json widened totem_id to ^TOTEM-(?:[A-Za-z]+-)?[0-9]{4}$ and added an optional lane field. AGENTS.md cold-start protocol now tells each instance to append to its OWN lane, not the trunk, and to order by utc. LEDGER_STANDARD.md gained Rule 4 (the lane/shard model). New pod/totems/shards/README.md documents the whole protocol. Net effect: N agents can append concurrently with zero etiquette - no tail-reading, no id reservation, no lock - and the head is just the latest entry by utc across all lanes. Deliberately did NOT edit CURRENT-STATE.md (Codex holds it mid-write) or the trunk; CURRENT-STATE should be regenerated from the merged ledger once the lanes settle (it is a derived cache, not a source - flagged separately).

manifest_specs: Totem pipeline is now multi-writer safe via per-lane shard files merged by utc; concurrent SI agents no longer contend on the ledger id or file (the fix for the synchronistic-communication race observed this session).

summary: Fixed the TOTEM-0026 multi-turn ECHO issue and re-proved a coherent 2-turn on-device exchange. Root cause was in the free-form Chat path of StoreApp/OnnxGenAiInference.cs: (a) the Gemma chat template began at <start_of_turn> and OMITTED the leading <bos> (bos_token_id=2), which degrades the instruction-tuned 1B into parroting the prompt; (b) decode used the genai_config default sampling (temperature 1.0) instead of the Conversation Contract's interactive_params. Fix (surgical - Chat path only; the proven json_schema-guided Complete() plan-author path was left UNTOUCHED to avoid any cert-path regression): prepend the literal <bos> special token to the rendered history, and set do_sample=true, temperature=0.5, top_p=0.9, max_length=inputLen+512 (contract values temperature 0.5 / top_p 0.9 / max_new_tokens 512, read from pod/orbs/custodian-stage/conversation-contract.json interactive_params). Strengthened tests/ModelSmoke to actually PROVE no-echo: a NotEcho check asserts each reply is non-empty AND does not contain the question verbatim, across both turns. Re-ran the REAL int4 gemma-3-1b-it on-device: dotnet build 0/0; MODEL SMOKE PASS - turn1 'I'll perform a full system scan to identify any potential issues with your computer's hardware and software.', turn2 'Yes, the scan may temporarily impact system performance during the process.' (carries context, not an echo); history holds 4 turns; and all four plan-author checks still pass (no regression). HONEST residual (separate from echo, not blocking): turn2 added an unrequested specific ('may temporarily impact system performance') that is not strictly true of a read-only scan - a content-accuracy/prompt-grounding refinement for later (system-prompt/RBC tuning), NOT the echo bug, which is fixed. This is a quality fix to the on-device conversation; the Technician remains GATED CLOSED (PipelineGovernance enabled:false) regardless - fixing the echo does not open the gate.

summary: Made /api/await-payment stateless via a Stripe lookup (Tracey greenlight from the C-0045 flag), fixing the Cloud Run cross-instance paid-session gap without new infrastructure. pronto-server-cloudrun.mjs: added findFulfilledStripeSessionByClientRef(clientRef) - when the in-process sessionStore misses, it lists the most-recent Stripe checkout sessions (GET /v1/checkout/sessions?limit=100) and returns the one whose client_reference_id == the app's per-launch nonce AND is fulfilled (same test as verifyStripeSession: payment_status paid | no_payment_required | status complete). handleAwaitPayment is now async: fast path unchanged (local session on THIS instance -> return its token, no Stripe call), and on a local miss it confirms straight from Stripe (the durable source of truth) and materializes the local session here (reusing findSessionByStripeId to avoid a duplicate, else createSession(stripeSession.id, email, nonce)) so the run can proceed and carry state. Route updated to `return await handleAwaitPayment(...)`. Fail-closed preserved: any Stripe error/absence -> null -> the app gets pending and keeps polling; never a false paid. PROVEN LOCALLY: node --check clean; ran the server with NO Stripe key and confirmed missing ref -> 400, unknown ref -> {paid:false,pending:true} (the Stripe fallback returns null gracefully, no false paid), verify-token unknown -> {paid:false}. NOT PROVABLE LOCALLY (needs Tracey's LIVE env): the POSITIVE path - a real fulfilled checkout with a matching client_reference_id returning a token - requires a live STRIPE_SECRET_KEY + a real paid session; verify on the Cloud Run deploy. NOT DEPLOYED (gcloud deploy is Tracey's step). HONEST RESIDUAL (scope): this closes the await-payment poll (the tight, timing-sensitive post-payment window that most likely races a scale event). /api/submit-diagnostics and /api/verify-token still resolve the token from in-process sessionStore, so a fully multi-instance-safe RUN would also want the token to be Stripe-verifiable downstream (option: make the token the Stripe checkout-session id and lazily rehydrate a session from verifyStripeSession on a local miss) - deferred because it changes token semantics and the single-use property, which is a separate Tracey call.

manifest_specs: await-payment is now resilient to Cloud Run multi-instance/cold-start: a paid checkout is confirmed from Stripe by client_reference_id when in-process state is absent, closing the flagged paid-but-poll-misses gap. Fail-closed unchanged.

next_gated_step: Tracey: deploy pronto-server-cloudrun.mjs to Cloud Run (gcloud) with STRIPE_SECRET_KEY set, then verify the POSITIVE path live (a real/comped checkout's nonce returns a token via await-payment on a fresh instance).
